title: Fair Enough? A map of the current limitations of the requirements to have fair algorithms.

bias_targets.methodology: Conceptual analysis using causal graphs and the historical 1973 Berkeley graduate admissions dataset to evaluate the limitations of observational metrics, Simpson's paradox, and direct versus indirect discrimination.
Theoretical evaluation of proxy variables, confounding, and indirect discrimination using the case study of Amazon's same-day delivery service coverage in Boston neighborhoods.
Conceptual analysis of the group aggregation problem, discussing the methodological challenges of discretizing continuous variables into thresholds to measure unjust discrimination.

Philosophical and theoretical evaluation of constitutive versus causal relationships, using religious affiliation to demonstrate the limitations of modeling human attributes as manipulable nodes in causal graphs.
